Legacy Expo InvoiceGenerate initializes superRateSnapshot to 10% (line 115) and only changes it when onboarding.super_rate_snapshot is truthy (lines 138-154). POST generateInvoice passes it as super_rate_snapshot (line 392); backend invoicing.services persists exact value (line 332), calculates super_base * rate/100 (lines 172-178). As at 2026 the Australian SG rate is 12%, but contractual super liability varies. Stale 10% default is a conditional financial accuracy issue in an exposed legacy invoice tool. Server currently does not replace with current statutory rate. S3 financial examples and legal classification needed.

findings.title: Legacy Expo invoice generator defaults superannuation to 10% despite Australia's current 12% SG rate.
findings.scenario: An eligible contractor or worker opens the legacy Expo invoice generator without an existing onboarding super-rate snapshot. The form starts at 10%. The app sends that percentage in the invoice payload; the legacy invoicing service trusts and persists it and calculates the generated superannuation line using that 10%. The actual 2026 standard SG rate is 12%, so a user who relies on the default may generate a short super request. This is a conditional calculation issue, not proof every contractor is SG-eligible or that every custom invoice must charge statutory SG.
findings.confidence: high for hardcoded default/source calculation; legal applicability conditional
findings.test_needed: New user with no onboarding super_rate_snapshot uses legacy InvoiceGenerate for an eligible 2026 invoice; assert suggested rate is current rate 12% (or explicitly configured award/agreement rate), correctly calculates amount, and backend does not silently accept stale default. Confirm historical invoice dates, contractor eligibility, intentionally different agreed rates and legacy vs new FinanceWorkspace paths.

owner_question.question: Should the legacy Expo invoice generator continue pre-populating a 10% superannuation rate for 2026 invoices?
